title: Park of Three
statementMd:
The Park of Three is a famous landmark in the Kingdom of Three. It contains 𝑛n magical pillars connected by 𝑚m *magical connections*. The pillars are numbered from 11 to 𝑛n. The 𝑖i-th connection links pillar 𝑢𝑖ui and pillar 𝑣𝑖vi, and all connections are bidirectional.

Believing that the number three holds protective power against evil forces, the park's architects ensured that every pillar is incident to exactly three connections. Note that a connection may link a pillar to itself. In such cases, the self-loop counts twice toward the number of pillar's incident connections.

Triangles formed by the pillars are the source of their protective power. Historically, these triangles successfully repelled evil forces hundreds of years ago. To assess the network's true resilience, you must determine its structural vulnerability.

Formally, three distinct pillars 𝑖,𝑗,𝑘i,j,k form a *triangle* if the connections (𝑖,𝑗)(i,j), (𝑗,𝑘)(j,k), and (𝑘,𝑖)(k,i) all exist. When a pillar is destroyed, all connections incident to it are removed. The *strength* of the park is defined as the minimum number 𝑠s such that destroying 𝑠s specific pillars eliminates all triangles. Please determine the strength 𝑠s and output the indices of 𝑠s pillars such that there will be no triangles after destroying them.

## Input

The first line contains an integer 𝑛n, representing the number of magical pillars in the park.

Followed by 𝑚=3𝑛2m=3n2 lines, the 𝑖i-th of which contains two integers 𝑢𝑖ui and 𝑣𝑖vi, representing the endpoints of the 𝑖i-th magical connection.

- 4≤𝑛≤2×1054≤n≤2×105, and 𝑛n is even.
- 1≤𝑢𝑖,𝑣𝑖≤𝑛1≤ui,vi≤n for all 1≤𝑖≤𝑚1≤i≤m.
- The network of magical connections may contain self-loops and multiple connections between the same pair of pillars.
- Each pillar is incident to exactly 33 connections, where each self-loop is counted twice toward this total.

## Output

On the first line, output the integer 𝑠s.

On the second line, output 𝑠s distinct integers representing the indices of the pillars to be destroyed. After removing these pillars and all incident connections, no triangles should remain.

If multiple solutions exist, output any of them. The indices may be printed in any order.

## Note

**Explanation for Sample 1**

The network of connections is shown in the figure below. There are 44 triangles formed by the pillars: (1,2,3)(1,2,3), (1,2,4)(1,2,4), (1,3,4)(1,3,4), and (2,3,4)(2,3,4). After destroying pillars 11 and 22, no triangle remains in the network. Any subset of {1,2,3,4}{1,2,3,4} of size 2 is also a valid solution.
